title: 拒绝“AI 垃圾代码”！LibreOffice 祭出最严 AI 编程新规：用大模型写代码，必须先过“人工解释”关
content:
As “one-click code generation” becomes part of developers’ daily routine, the open-source community is facing a hidden crisis: black-box logic, hard-to-maintain “spaghetti code,” and insufficiently reviewed “AI slop” are quietly eroding the foundations of software engineering. In response to this industry pain point, The Document Foundation (TDF), the maintainer of the long-established open-source office suite LibreOffice, has formally drawn a red line and announced extremely strict new rules for large language models (LLMs) and AI-assisted programming.
Core red line: not just disclosure, but “understanding every line”
TDF’s new rules are not a blanket ban on AI. Instead, they use a tightly controlled process to ensure that AI remains a tool, not a way to shift responsibility. The new rules set out four hard requirements:
1. Prior approval and mandatory disclosure: Contributors must obtain approval before using LLMs to assist development, and when submitting code (a commit), they must clearly disclose their use of AI tools.
2. A strict “human explanation” obligation: For patches completed with the help of LLMs, contributors must be able to clearly explain, in their own words, the principle and purpose of every line of modified code. This means the era of “copy, paste, and submit” is completely over.
3. Defining AI no-go zones: The use of LLMs is explicitly prohibited for writing commit messages, code comments, bug reports, and messages to other developers.
4. Sensitive-area isolation: Some areas of the core codebase are directly designated as off-limits for LLM use, cutting off the potential risks posed by AI-generated content at the physical level.
Deeper logic: embrace efficiency, but defend the value of “human code”
In its statement, TDF candidly acknowledged that LibreOffice itself does not contain any AI features, and that AI-assisted programming is already an unavoidable reality in the software development community. The foundation has not completely banned AI; as long as the final contributed code is of acceptable quality, it will still be accepted.
However, behind this “limited openness” is a deep commitment to the essence of software engineering. Code is not just instructions that a machine can run; it is the crystallization of human logic and a contract for team collaboration. If developers cannot even restate the logic of AI-generated code in their own words, then the maintainability, security, and future iteration of that code will be a disaster. TDF’s move is precisely intended to build a solid firewall between “AI-driven efficiency” and “code quality control.”
Industry insight: the open-source community’s “battle to protect code quality” is in full swing
LibreOffice’s choice is by no means an isolated case; it is a microcosm of the broader trend in software development today. Even Linux founder Linus Torvalds has clearly stated that his openness to AI-assisted programming is premised on developers strictly following the rules and taking ultimate responsibility.
With the spread of AI coding assistants (such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and others), open-source projects stand at a crossroads: should they allow AI-generated content to run rampant and cause projects to decay, or establish strict review mechanisms to ensure long-term health? TDF’s new rules provide a highly valuable reference model—technology can assist thinking, but responsibility must never be outsourced.
In the future, outsiders will closely watch how LibreOffice’s code reviewers put these rules into practice. But one thing is certain: when “being able to explain the code you wrote” once again becomes a basic quality for open-source contributors, software development is returning to its core values: clear logic, reliable engineering quality, and a sense of reverence for every line of code.

report.summary: LibreOffice 严管 AI 写代码，须逐行人工解释
report.background: 随着 GitHub Copilot、Cursor 等 AI 编程助手普及，开源社区出现黑箱逻辑、难以维护的“面条代码”和审查不足的“AI 垃圾代码”。LibreOffice 维护方 The Document Foundation 因此发布严格新规，试图在提升开发效率与守住代码质量之间划清边界。
key_points: TDF 并非全面禁止 AI，而是要求贡献者使用大模型前先获批准，并在提交代码时明确披露所用 AI 工具。
最严一条是人工解释义务：借助 LLM 完成的补丁，开发者须用自己的话讲清每一行改动原理和目的，复制粘贴提交不再可行。
AI 禁区明确：提交信息、代码注释、缺陷报告和开发者沟通消息不得用 LLM 代写，防止沟通与文档被黑箱内容污染。
核心代码库部分敏感区域被设为 LLM 禁用区，从物理层面隔离 AI 生成内容带来的安全与维护风险。
TDF 表示只要最终代码质量达标仍会接收，体现有限开放：AI 可提效，但责任、逻辑与可维护性必须由人承担。
report.impact: 对 AI 行业，AI 编程工具将从“生成即用”转向“可解释、可审计”，厂商需补足代码来源追踪与合规能力。对开发者，使用大模型不再是免责牌，需具备代码审查和复述能力，提交门槛提高。对普通用户，短期可能降低 AI 垃圾代码进入关键软件的几率，长期有利于开源软件安全与可持续维护。
report.tools: 可跟进 TDF 官方公告与 LibreOffice 开发者邮件列表；实践上可用 git 提交模板强制披露 AI 使用，配合 SonarQube、Semgrep 做静态检查，并用 GitHub Copilot、Cursor 时保留对话与变更记录以便人工解释。
